meta.title: The Belief You Cannot Buy
meta.theme: why belief cannot be adopted at will, and where a demand on a believer can fall

format.format_verified: 2026-09: recent CAT papers set Para Summary among the non-negative verbal questions; re-verify against each new official paper

apex.claim: Belief cannot be adopted at will because a belief aims at truth and a state produced by an inducement would be answering to the inducement instead; what remains is indirect control over reading and consulting, and that is where a demand on a believer can sensibly fall.
apex.scope: The direct voluntary adoption of belief; the paragraph allows indirect control and locates legitimate demands there, without saying what anyone must do.

meta.learning_objective: resist converting a claim about where a demand can fall into a statement of what that demand requires

quality.adversarial_review: The live rival is the option imposing a duty to read widely and consult opponents. The paragraph says where a demand can sensibly fall, which is a claim about the possible location of an obligation, and then observes that this place is narrower than the demands people usually make; it never states the obligation itself. The arm-raising option is the illustration that opens the argument. The option explaining belief by upbringing and circumstance replaces a claim about what a belief is with a claim about what causes beliefs, and the second sentence rules that out by saying the reason is not weakness of will but the kind of state a belief is.

source.usage_note: Original composition in CAT register for CAT OS. General philosophical reasoning about the involuntariness of belief; no specific text adapted. Personal study only.

meta.reviewer_notes: A constitutive explanation that is easily swapped for a causal one, closing on a location claim that is easily swapped for a duty. Three distortion families: addition (the duty stated), structure (the illustration promoted), scope (a different kind of explanation substituted).

sentences.text: Offer a person money to raise an arm and the arm goes up; offer the same money to believe that it is raining and nothing whatever happens.
The reason is not weakness of will but the kind of state a belief is: a belief aims at truth, and a state produced by an inducement would be answering to the inducement instead.
Nobody can both believe something and hold in mind that the reason they believe it has nothing to do with whether it is so.
What is left is indirect control: what a person reads, whom they consult, which questions they let themselves keep open.
That is where a demand on a believer can sensibly fall, and it is a narrower place than the demands people usually make of one another's opinions.

ideal_summary: Belief cannot be taken up at will, because a belief aims at truth and one bought by an inducement would not, so the only demands that can sensibly reach a believer concern what they read and whom they consult.

builder.prompt: In one sentence: why does the paragraph say belief cannot be chosen, and what does it say follows for demands on believers?

checks.ask: Does your sentence explain why belief resists the will, rather than only that it does?
checks.kept: Good. The reason is what a belief is for: it answers to truth, and a state bought with money would be answering to the money.
checks.drifted: Reporting that we cannot decide to believe gives the phenomenon without the account. The paragraph's work is in the second and third sentences.

checks.ask: Does your sentence say where a demand can fall, or has it stated the demand?
checks.kept: Exactly right. The author marks out a region in which an obligation could sensibly sit and declines to fill it with any particular duty.
checks.drifted: A duty to read widely or to consult those who disagree is the obvious content to pour into that region, and the paragraph pours none. It says only where such a demand could land.

checks.ask: Is your explanation about what a belief is, or about what causes people's beliefs?
checks.kept: Well held. The second sentence rules out weakness of will and points at the nature of the state, which is a different sort of explanation from upbringing or circumstance.
checks.drifted: Saying that beliefs are formed by background replaces a claim about what belief is with a claim about where beliefs come from, and the paragraph explicitly sets the second aside.

question.stem: Which option best captures the essence of the paragraph?

options.A: Since only indirect control is available, everyone has a standing duty to read widely and to consult those who disagree with them before they settle on an opinion.
options.B: Belief cannot be taken up at will because it aims at truth, so the only demands that can sensibly reach a believer concern what they read and whom they consult.
options.C: A person offered money will raise an arm on request but cannot in the same way produce the belief that it happens to be raining outside the window now.
options.D: People cannot simply decide what to believe, because their convictions are formed by upbringing and by circumstance rather than by any choice of their own.

explanation.paragraph_meaning: Pay someone to lift an arm and they lift it. Pay them to believe it is raining and nothing happens at all. The paragraph says this is not a failure of nerve. A belief is the sort of state that answers to how things are, and one produced by a payment would be answering to the payment, which is a different thing. You cannot hold a belief while also keeping in view that your reason for holding it has nothing to do with its truth. What is left is the roundabout route: choosing what to read, whom to ask, which questions to leave open. That is the only place where a demand on someone's beliefs can sensibly land, and it is a smaller place than the demands we usually make.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option keeps the reason belief resists the will, that it aims at truth, and the conclusion about where a demand can sensibly fall, which is the reading and consulting the fourth sentence describes. It states a location for demands rather than a demand.

distractors.why_wrong: The paragraph says where a demand on a believer can sensibly fall, and adds that this is narrower than what people usually demand. It never issues the demand, and a duty binding everyone is exactly the kind of requirement the last clause is measuring against.
distractors.seductive_element: It supplies the obvious content for the space the argument opens, and an ethical conclusion feels like the natural destination of a philosophical paragraph.
distractors.thinking_mistake: Filling a space an author marked out, and mistaking the filling for what the author said.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the opening illustration. It sets up the puzzle the next two sentences explain and the last one draws a conclusion from, and none of that survives here.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the only concrete image in an abstract paragraph, and it is the sentence a reader has most firmly in mind by the end.
distractors.thinking_mistake: Reporting the demonstration a paragraph opens with rather than the account it was opened to motivate.

distractors.why_wrong: The paragraph explains the impossibility by what a belief is, and says in terms that the reason is not weakness of will. Upbringing and circumstance are a story about where beliefs come from, which is a different kind of explanation and not the one offered.
distractors.seductive_element: It reaches the same headline, that belief is not chosen, by a route most readers already find persuasive.
distractors.thinking_mistake: Accepting an option because its conclusion matches, without checking that the reason behind it is the author's.

explanation.reading_habit: When an author says where an obligation could sensibly sit, check whether they ever said what it requires. Marking out a space is not the same as filling it.

mentor.challenge: The paragraph opens a space for a demand and refuses to say what the demand is. One option says it for the author.
mentor.takeaway: You can choose what you read. You cannot choose what reading it makes you believe.
